title: Preservation during a two-pass scan
statement: Let $A$ and $\Gamma$ be types, let $x,w$ be lists over $\Gamma$, let $i$ be one of four work-tape indices, and let $\delta_f,\delta_b:A\times\Gamma\to A\times\Gamma$ be transition maps. Suppose a configuration $c$ of the four-tape scan machine on input $x$ is in forward phase with state $a$, and tape $i$, at every offset $z$ from its head with $-1\le z\le |w|$, contains the corresponding symbol of $w$ (and is blank where that word has no symbol). If the forward-and-backward scan of $w$ from state $a$ returns the pair $(b,w)$, then after $2|w|+2$ steps the machine is in configuration $c$ with state changed to the completed phase carrying $b$. It has not entered any completed phase earlier, and through that time tape $i$'s head remains between its initial position minus one and its initial position plus $|w|$, while every other work-tape head stays fixed.
